title: "Minsoo Cho"
---

<div class="page__content">

I am a Ph.D. candidate in Economics at Florida State University, where I also earned my M.S. in Economics. Before FSU, I completed my M.A. and B.A. in Economics at the University of Seoul, advised by Dr. Hyelim Son.

My research sits at the intersection of public, labor, and health economics, with a focus on how income support programs shape the well-being of older adults. My current work studies the effects of South Korea's Basic Pension reform on the consumption, labor supply, and mental health of elderly recipients.

My broader research interests extend to applied microeconomics more generally — from labor market outcomes such as divorce among dual-income couples to survival analysis in the movie screening market — reflecting a continued interest in using empirical methods to answer questions with real policy relevance.

Alongside my research, I have taught and assisted courses in microeconomics, macroeconomics, and econometrics at both Florida State University and the University of Seoul.

</div>
